    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    La conferenza stampa di Gennaro Gattuso in occasione della sfida casalinga contro il Lecce.

    La sosta per gli impegni delle nazionali è finalmente giunta al termine, e le squadre di Serie A sono pronte a scendere in campo per la dodicesima giornata. In occasione del prossimo turno, la Lazio ospiterà allo stadio Olimpico di Roma il Lecce di Di Francese per la sfida in programma sabato 21 novembre alle ore 15:00. Dalla sala stampa del Training Center di Formello, il mister Gattuso è intervenuto in conferenza stampa per presentare il match contro i salentini.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Su Frattesi non devo riflettere, ha fatto tutto col gruppo, sta bene e a livello strumentale non ha nulla. Se oggi arriva e ha il raffreddore vediamo, ma ha fatto tutto. Isaksen e Provstgaard hanno fatto un lavoro in palestra come Dele-Bashiru e Belahyane. Tutti i giocatori hanno lavorato con noi. Zaccagni sta lavorando sul campo, c’è ancora un po’ di edema, ma riesce a gestire. Nuno ha cominciato riabilitazione in piscina con Sutalo. Marusic ha avuto una piccola ricaduta, sulla ricaduta che ha avuto un mese fa. Settimana prossima valutiamo in che condizione sono. Gli altri sono tutti a disposizione. Cataldi ieri non si è allenato, ha avuto un piccolo problema all’adduttore, ma pensiamo non sia nulla di grave.

    Si pensa a domani, non a quello che dobbiamo fare dopo. Giochiamo contro una squadra solida e allenata bene, ha dieci punti in classifica. Ha vinto con l’Udinese e col Venezia, una squadra molto insidiosa sui calci piazzati. Dobbiamo prenderli con le pinze. Sta a noi come sempre. Servirà mentalità e voglia di stare in campo e giocare a ritmi elevati. È una partita molto difficile.

    It has been revealed that ci può stare, ma per come giochiamo il modulo non c’entra niente. Dipende solo come andare a prendere gli avversari in pressing. L’importante è andare a occupare le posizioni libere, cambia poco. Conta la voglia, la partecipazione e la mentalità. Per questo, si può fare tutto, se andate a vedere quando facciamo pressioni stiamo solo con un vertice. Conta poco il modulo.

    Non devo entrare solo nella sua, devo entrare nella testa di tutti. Lui è un giocatore importante ma ci sono anche gli altri. Bisogna capire cosa significa giocare poco. Sia Dele-Bashiru e Lazzari ci danno sempre un contributo quando entrano. Albert quando sta bene è un giocatore di altissimo livello. Domani tanti di loro che hanno trovato poco spazio avranno la possibilità di giocare dal primo minuto, ma sono tranquillo. L’importante è avere la consapevolezza che i giocatori hanno una buona condizione.

    Per come sono fatto io non sono mai sereno, fa parte del mio modo di essere. Ho la consapevolezza che sono ragazzi che non si risparmiano mai. La qualità di corsa è alta, sono tutti ad un ottimo livello e questo mi riempie d’orgoglio. Domani dovremo far parlare in campo e metterlo in pratica.

    Quando ho detto che non abbiamo niente da perdere mi hanno guardato storto, ma altri ragionamenti si fanno nelle ultime partite. Noi dobbiamo vivere partita dopo partita. Giochiamocela domani, poi vedremo dove si arriva. Io alleno una squadra che in questo momento deve vivere alla giornata. Le partite bisogna giocarle, importante è che non sbagliamo a livello di atteggiamento.

    Ieri abbiamo visto la partita contro il Napoli, serve la mentalità, il guardarsi. Il veleno su ogni palla, quello deve essere nel nostro DNA. Siamo andati là e potevamo fare più di un gol, poi nel primo quarto d’ora potevamo perderla, poi siamo tornati in partita. Non bisogna dimenticare cosa ci ha portato qui. Se siamo qui è perchè giochiamo da squadra, perché non si molla di un centimetro. Poi si può sempre sbagliare, lo accettiamo sempre, l’importante è che non manchi la voglia di soffrire in campo. La squadra ha avuto miglioramenti, a volte siamo usciti dal campo e Mandas ci ha dato una mano, ma a livello di personalità abbiamo fatto un step importante. Bisogna lavorare sempre con personalità, senza dimenticare da dove siamo partiti.

    Sources indicate that non mi piace fare il gitano, amo andare in giro e toccare con mano le mentalità di altri paesi. La mia crescita viene anche da tutti i giri che ho fatto. Noi italiani pensiamo sempre di essere i più forti, ma su tantissime cose nel calcio riesci a mettere dentro anche delle altre culture. Non penso se dovrò rimanere o meno, penso a quello che dovrò fare oggi. Sembra che io sia qui da dieci anni, mi sento a mio agio qui. Spero di rimanerci a lungo, difficilmente puoi trovare posti così.

    Ho grande fiducia, vedo quello che fanno e come lavorano. Doekhi si è trovato fuori, ma quando ha giocato ha sempre fatto bene. C’è grande fiducia sul reparto difensivo. Pedraza non ha mai giocato, ma ha messo minutaggio da subentrato. C’è fiducia nei loro confronti. Romano? Ci sta che certe volte possa soffrire in fase difensiva, ma l’esperienza si fa giocando, con questo tipo di partite che sta giocando. Ci sta che possa subire questo tipo di partite. Siamo contenti che abbia rinnovato, ha grande voglia e senso di appartenenza.

    It has been revealed that lui in questo momento per la mentalità che ha, può giocare anche a centrocampo e in difesa. Ha una convinzione e una condizione fisica incredibile. Lui può fare l’ala e l’ha dimostrato a Napoli, giocando con voglia e mentalità, ma può giocare ovunque. Non sono d’accordo con voi, avete massacrato Pinamonti dopo Napoli, si è speso tanto nel primo tempo. Nella ripresa abbiamo sofferto tutti, lui è in grandissima crescita.

    According to recent reports, saranno affari loro se giocano alla playstation, non so nemmeno di che stai parlando. Non mi creo questo problema. Questo fa parte dell’essere professionista, di avere amor proprio del proprio lavoro. Non mi permetterei mai di chiedere ad un giocatore se ha dormito o meno. Vediamo domani mattina, ci sarà la colazione tutti insieme e mi metterò là concentrato e vedremo se qualcuno avrà fatto le ore piccole o meno.

    Con lui abbiamo parlato, sapevo dove andare a parare. Si toccava con mano che tutto quello che era stato fatto non gli era entrato bene nella testa, ma ci sta: veniva da un calcio totalmente diverso. Tutte le nostre proposte erano arabo per lui, lo sapevo già. Da lì ha svoltato, gli ho detto che doveva chiedere ciò che non capiva e siamo rimasti di più in campo. Dopo gli è venuto più facile. Ci ha fatto vincere qualche partita, ma ci stava che all’inizio, avendo fatto cose totalmente diverse, avesse difficoltà. Sono sicuro che domani farà una grande partita.

    Recent findings suggest that non è facile, anche un mese fa siamo stati fermi venti giorni. Non passano mai. Sappiamo quello che abbiamo dovuto fare, non è facile. Ci sono anche Champions, Europa e Conference. È una cosa di UEFA e FIFA che devono sedersi per mettersi d’accordo coi club, altrimenti non se ne esce fuori. Quando giocavo, a fine anno controllavo e avevo fatto 52 partite. Il problema è che adesso si gioca anche il venerdì e il sabato alle 15. I tempi di recupero sono diversi. Non siamo le persone adatte per lamentarci per quello che guadagnamo. I salari dei giocatori sono importanti, non vengo qua a lamentarmi.

    Sources indicate that quella di domani. C’è poco da rispondere. I tre punti di domani sono uguali ai prossimi, non abbiamo priorità. L’avversario è diverso, ma per me è troppo difficile dirti cosa penso. Io penso alla gara di domani, poi vedremo cosa succederà a Torino. Come se adesso mi chiedessi del derby, so che tutti ci aspettano perché vogliono che vinciamo il derby, ma pensa come ci arrivo se ci comincio a pensare ora.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Isaksen è proposto a 2,75; per il Lecce, il primo gol in Serie A di Geubbels è offerto a 5,00.

    In a recent development, la Lazio torna in campo contro il Lecce con l’obiettivo di restare imbattuta e conquistare la decima vittoria in Serie A. Secondo quanto riportato da Agipronews, All’Olimpico i biancocelesti partono favoriti nelle quote: il successo della squadra di Gennaro Gattuso è offerto a 1,38, mentre il gol di Tijjani Noslin si gioca a 2,25.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    According to recent reports, secondo i betting analyst di Sisal e Betflag, citati da Agipronews, la vittoria del Lecce è proposta a 8,00. Il pareggio si colloca invece tra 4,75 e 4,90. Per la squadra di Gattuso, la sfida arriva dopo la pausa del campionato.

    Nei diciannove precedenti all’Olimpico, i salentini hanno vinto soltanto due volte. Il bilancio degli ultimi undici confronti tra le due squadre è però in equilibrio: quattro successi per parte e tre pareggi.

    La Lazio ha segnato 25 reti nelle prime undici giornate. Nello stesso arco di campionato aveva fatto meglio soltanto nella stagione 2017/2018, quando i gol erano stati 31.

    Nei mercati sulle reti, l’Over è offerto a 1,50 e precede l’Under, proposto a 2,40. Anche il Goal, a 1,72, ha una quota inferiore rispetto al No Goal, fissato a 2,00.

    #61983. Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

    📅 14 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 27m • 📚 Deep Dive (5406 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

    📅 14 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5406 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.
    • Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.
    • The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

    Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

    The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

    LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

    Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

    In a recent development, peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

    Industry observers note that “We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

    “We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

    Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

    Mowbray noted: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

    “Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

    The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

    However, Wolves scored the first goal of the upcoming campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

    "A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

    Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

    The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

    Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

    "It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

    Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

    However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

    Wolverhampton: Bentley, Trippier, Mosquera, Toti Gomes, Wolfe, Lopez, Andre Trindade, Munetsi, Rodrigo Gomes, Armstrong, Mane.Subs used: Jiménez 60 (Mateus Mané), ‌Doyle ‌67 (Rodrigo Gomes), ⁠Tchatchoua 67 (Trippier), Pedro Lima 79 (André),Chirewa 79 (Møller Wolfe)Scorers: M. Munetsi 18, R. Jiménez 90+3penYellow card: Mateus Mané 52Blackburn: Toth, Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering, Montgomery, Forshaw, Morishita, Cantwell, Afolayan, Gudjohnsen.Subs used: Sam Morsy 55 (Forshaw), Fevrier 68 (Afolayan), Ohashi ‌68 (Cantwell), Garrett ​79 (Gudjohnsen), ⁠Yuri Ribeiro79 (Morishita)Scorers: ⁠S. McLoughlin 27, A. Gudjohnsen 48Yellow card: Pickering ​34, Cantwell 35, ‌Forshaw 45Attendance: 30,984Referee: Farai ⁠Hallam.

    “I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”.

    Industry observers note that “We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”.

    According to recent reports, “It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is crucial. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”.

    “Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”.

    Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc.

    Recent findings suggest that “Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case. Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”.

    “Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”.

    It has been revealed that bentley spills the corner but gets a free-kick. Moments later, the referee blows his whistle for the final time and the game ends level at 2-2. A dramatic opening night of the new Championship season at Molineux. If the Championship continues in this vein all season, it will be one hell of a year.

    Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

    He sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

    Industry observers note that LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

    Sources indicate that it just had to be. Jimenez rescues Wolves from the penalty spot.

    Drama on the opening night of the campaign.

    Relief for Wolves, heartbreak for Blackburn.

    According to recent reports, late drama at Molineux! The cross is sent in from the left and the ball strikes the arm Alebiosu on the edge of the box. Was it inside or outside the penalty area? It is definitely handball but was it outside the box? It was very, very close but there is no VAR in the Championship so the penalty will stand.

    Recent findings suggest that four added minutes. Are we on the verge of seeing the first shock of the new Championship season on opening night?

    Four minutes added. Not even a reaction from the home crowd.

    Wolves are desperately running out of time and Blackburn still look comfortable.

    Home fans are beginning to filter out slowly.

    Mosquera is still struggling but he has come back on whilst limping around. I cannot imagine there will be too much in terms of added time, either three or four minutes would be my guess, no more.

    Ohashi is played in behind and goes down under a challenge from Toti on the edge of the Wolves box but those appeals are waved away.

    Mosquera has gone down again and he may not be able to continue as he receives treatment on the sidelines. Wolves may be ending this game down to 10 men.

    Fevrier’s shot from outside the Wolves penalty area is blocked and spins behind for a corner in front of the travelling Blackburn fans. The corner comes to nothing.

    Wolves struggling to create anything of note even with Jimenez’s introduction.

    Centre-back Mosquera has gone up front but appears to be struggling with an injury. He’s jogged back to his natural position now.

    Rovers fans still making the noise.

    Wolves do not at the moment look like scoring an equaliser.

    Blackburn are looking pretty comfortable right now defending their lead and counter-attacking effectively.

    Wolves are pushing to find an equaliser but are struggling to carve out many genuine opportunities.

    Ohashi is penalised for a foul on F Lopez not far outside the Blackburn penalty area and that was pretty harsh on Ohashi. Jimenez is lining this one up as is F Lopez.

    Recent findings suggest that can he inspire a comeback? Wolves and Peixoto will certainly hope so.

    Munetsi, the scorer of Wolves’ goal, has a shot deflected from the edge of the box and it goes behind for a corner. Gudjohnsen, the scorer of Blackburn’s second, heads away at the front post.

    Blackburn are the first to turn to their bench as one experienced midfielder replaces another with Morsy coming on for Forshaw.

    Wow! What a start to the second half. Blackburn have turned it around, Tony Mowbray clearly inspired his troops at half time.

    Molineux is silenced now with Blackburn fans making all the noise. Some home supporters were still taking their seats as Gudjohnsen turned the ball home.

    The first half is brought to a close at Molineux and an engaging opening 45 minutes of the new Championship season results in this game being level at 1-1 at the break. Munetsi put Wolves in front before McLoughlin equalised for Blackburn.

    Mane wins it back for his side on the edge of his own penalty area and drives forward. He takes it across the halfway line before feeding a lovely pass to his right to find Armstrong, whose shot is blocked.

    Mane comes close to a stunner. Trippier rolls the ball across the face of the penalty area to 18-year-old Mane, who takes on the shot first time but his effort goes just over the bar.

    What a response from Blackburn.

    Molineux briefly stunned into silence. A slight delay from the fans celebrating the header as well.

    The first booking of the Championship season goes the way of Blackburn left-back Pickering. It is a pretty simple decision for the referee as Pickering cynically pulls back R Gomes, who had spun him, and rightly receives a yellow card.

However, Alebiosu, with Mane not far behind him, puts it behind for a corner. Trippier delivers and the Blackburn keeper makes a meal of it, missing his punch out but then scrambles back towards his own goal to gather the loose ball.

Morishita clips in the cross from the right to the near post, where McLoughlin meets it first and guides a powerful header into the far corner. Two goals in the opening half an hour of the latest Championship season.

    Sources indicate that blackburn are getting great joy down their right through Alebiosu and Morishita, with the latter winning them a corner as Toti is forced to head behind from a cross. Pickering sends it into a good area and the touch comes off the head of Munetsi, whose header loops into the air and goes just over his own bar for another corner on the other side.

    Cantwell’s delivery to the far post is headed away.

    A cool finish from the midfielder after a bit of a drab start from the home side.

    That will please the new Wolves boss. Such a simple move but the home side ripped Blackburn wide open with two passes.

    Work to do for the visitors now who had probably started the better of the two teams before the opener.

    Recent findings suggest that wolves fans make their feelings about VAR known following the goal. No VAR in the Championship of course but no VAR was needed for that anyway. A perfectly good goal.

    In a recent development, mane cuts inside from the left onto his preferred right foot and curls a dangerous ball into the box that is punched away by Toth in the Blackburn goal. 18-year-old Mane was one of very few bright spots for Wolves last season and in many ways it is a surprise that no Premier League teams have lured him back to the top flight quite yet. That could though still happen before the deadline.

    The first goal of the Championship season comes against the run of play. It is a clinical, ruthless goal that comes from an incisive pass and clinical finish. The pass is fed through by F Lopez to pick out the run of Munetsi, who is cool, calm and collected as he finishes past Toth. Blackburn had been the better side up until that point but Wolves take the lead at Molineux.

    "A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

    Sources indicate that A shot on target for Blackburn but an easy save in the end. Alebiosu, who has looked good in these early stages, drives down Blackburn’s right before cutting it back to Morishita on the edge of the box. Morishita takes one touch before shooting but his effort is tame and straight at Bentley.

    Blackburn have definitely been the better side in these early exchanges, dominating possession and looking a threat going forward.

    Blackburn may be heavy underdogs tonight but they have settled down well away at one of the favourites to get promoted. Tony Mowbray may well be seeing this as a good time to play Wolves away.

    Alebiosu shows quick feet down Blackburn’s right and clips a cross to the back post, where Afolayan meets it but his header is just off target.

    Recent findings suggest that safe to say the doom and gloom of last season appears to have lifted at Molineux. The home fans in fine voice early on here.

    By contrast, Kieran Trippier’s first touch of the season is greeted by loud boos by the travelling Blackburn supporters.

    In fact, every Trippier touch is greeted by a chorus of boos. Will they keep that up all game?

    They’ve certainly not forgotten his Burnley connection.

    New managers and new signings galore. This should be a fascinating spectacle.

    It has been revealed that he may not be in the starting XI tonight but Jimenez is being serenaded by the home fans on his return to Wolves after a few years away at Fulham. Jimenez and his wife have paid for 5,000 scarves for the Wolves fans tonight.

    Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray did say ahead of the game that Wolves have not been used to winning games over the last 12 months so can the visitors take advantage of that tonight? Blackburn are underdogs tonight and not too much is expected of them this season so surely they have nothing to lose this evening?

    Due to his Burnley ties, fresh Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

    In a recent development, after Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

    Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

    When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager fresh to English football, it proved a vintage season.

    Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

    Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

    Sources indicate that “I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

    “There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”.

    In a recent development, our experts have been having their say ahead of the newly introduced Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:.

    Industry observers note that it is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

    The boys are in the Black Country 👋 #WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/WjuGwrxYtQ.

    Saturday:Bolton vs PrestonBristol City vs MillwallCharlton vs DerbyMiddlesbrough vs LincolnNorwich vs West BromPortsmouth vs QPRStoke vs SwanseaSheffield United vs Birmingham.

    ☝️ One change from Port Vale🇳🇴 Wolfe in at LB🇪🇸 Hugo misses out with minor groin issueOur line-up for tonight's @EFL Championship opener 📋 pic.twitter.com/oRpIymUw1k.

    Sources indicate that the 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are upcoming playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

    In a recent development, wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

    Industry observers note that “I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

    “It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our major goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”.

    Industry observers note that they have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

    Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

    Recent findings suggest that “I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray stated. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”.

    It has been revealed that these sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

    Latest Update: Lazio-Lecce, Fascetti: biancocelesti favoriti, ma serve attenzione

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Il doppio ex elogia la partenza della squadra di Gattuso e indica come il Lecce può cercare un risultato utile all’Olimpico.
    • Per Eugenio Fascetti, la Lazio è nettamente favorita contro il Lecce nella sfida di domani alle 15 all’Olimpico.
    • CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Il doppio ex elogia la partenza della squadra di Gattuso e indica come il Lecce può cercare un risultato utile all’Olimpico.

    Per Eugenio Fascetti, la Lazio è nettamente favorita contro il Lecce nella sfida di domani alle 15 all’Olimpico. Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta del Mezzogiorno, Il doppio ex, però, avverte che i giallorossi dovranno giocare tutte le proprie carte per cercare un risultato utile. Elogia inoltre l’avvio dei biancocelesti, pur indicando nell’Inter la sua favorita per lo scudetto.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Fascetti ha allenato il Lecce dalla stagione 1983/1984 alla 1985/1986. Con il presidente Franco Jurlano, il direttore sportivo Mimmo Cataldo e i calciatori della stagione 1984/1985 conquistò la prima promozione del club salentino in Serie A. Da giocatore aveva vestito anche la maglia della Lazio nel 1964/1965; dopo l’esperienza a Lecce, guidò i biancocelesti nel 1986/1987 e nel 1987/1988.

    Sources indicate that A Roma ottenne prima la salvezza tra i cadetti, nonostante una penalizzazione iniziale di nove punti, poi la promozione in A. A 88 anni, dopo una vita trascorsa nel calcio tra campo e panchina, l’allenatore viareggino continua a seguire con attenzione la massima serie italiana e non solo.

    Industry observers note that fascetti conserva un legame con entrambe le piazze: «Ho splendidi ricordi delle esperienze vissute in entrambe le piazze». Ripensando alla promozione leccese, aggiunge: «Due avventure che rammento con molto piacere. A Lecce, con un grande gruppo di lavoro, dalla dirigenza allo staff, dai calciatori ad ogni collaboratore, raggiungemmo un traguardo che tutti, nel Salento, sognavano. Fu una cavalcata straordinaria, come del resto i festeggiamenti di popolo che seguirono, coinvolgendo un intero territorio.».

    Sources indicate that A quel traguardo Fascetti affianca il ricordo della morte di Michele Lorusso e Ciro Pezzella: «In giallorosso, purtroppo, ho vissuto anche un grave lutto, la tragica morte di Michele e di Ciro (le bandiere Lorusso e Pezzella ndr), che ancora oggi, a distanza di oltre 40 anni da quel maledetto 2 dicembre 1983, mi procura dolore solo a parlarne. Anche con la Lazio, però, ci siamo tolti delle belle soddisfazioni».

    Recent findings suggest that nel giudizio di Fascetti, il percorso del Lecce rispecchia quello di una squadra chiamata a lottare fino alla fine per restare in Serie A: «Il Lecce sta effettuando il cammino che compete ad uno schieramento che ha l’obiettivo di lottare sino alla fine per cercare di meritare la permanenza». Sugli alti e bassi precisa: «Per le formazioni costruite per salvarsi, è scontato che vadano messi in conto degli alti e bassi. Non potrebbe essere diversamente. I giallorossi sono in linea con le aspettative e dovranno battagliare con i denti per provare a compiere l’ennesima impresa sportiva degli ultimi anni. La sofferenza fa parte del dna degli appassionati salentini».

    Il presidente Saverio Sticchi Damiani e gli altri soci cercano di conciliare i risultati con un calcio sostenibile e conti in ordine. Finora, secondo Fascetti, ci sono riusciti. L’ex tecnico considera questa strada necessaria per i club di provincia: «Per le piccole realtà di provincia non ci sono alternative».

    Sources indicate that il paragone di Fascetti va alla gestione che conobbe a Lecce: «Ai miei tempi, Jurlano e Cataldo si sono dimostrati bravissimi a regalare a più riprese la serie A al Lecce a costi limitati. Due autentici campioni. L’attuale proprietà si muove lungo la medesima direttrice ed è la scelta giusta, anche se i tifosi, in quanto tali, vorrebbero soffrire di meno».

    #61966. Fresh manager bounce? How Mauricio Pochettino fared in his first match in charge of previous clubs

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (683 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Empireofthekop ↗ Open Full Page

    Fresh manager bounce? How Mauricio Pochettino fared in his first match in charge of previous clubs

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Empireofthekop

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Liverpool will be wary of the threat of ‘latest manager bounce’ on Sunday when they face a Manchester United team now under the management of Mauricio Pochettino.
    • Having sacked Michael Carrick last Thursday, the Red Devils moved swiftly to appoint the Argentine as his successor, with their new head coach signing off from a similar role with the United States with a 2-0 win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League.
    • The Old Trafford outfit enjoyed an immediate upsurge in form when their former midfielder replaced Ruben Amorim back in January, but how has the new man in charge fared in his first game at his five previous spells as a club boss?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Liverpool will be wary of the threat of ‘latest manager bounce’ on Sunday when they face a Manchester United team now under the management of Mauricio Pochettino.

    Having sacked Michael Carrick last Thursday, the Red Devils moved swiftly to appoint the Argentine as his successor, with their new head coach signing off from a similar role with the United States with a 2-0 win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League.

    The Old Trafford outfit enjoyed an immediate upsurge in form when their former midfielder replaced Ruben Amorim back in January, but how has the new man in charge fared in his first game at his five previous spells as a club boss?

    Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Espanyol were in the LaLiga relegation zone when Pochettino took charge almost 18 years ago, and his first task seemed a daunting one against city rivals Barcelona, who’d end the season as treble winners under Pep Guardiola.

    The Argentine had only two training sessions to implement his methods before the Copa Del Rey derby fixture, but his new team claimed an impressive share of the spoils on home turf before narrowly losing the second leg 3-2 at Camp Nou. A few weeks later, he masterminded a shock league victory at the home of their arch-rivals.

    The Saints’ decision to axe the popular Nigel Adkins mid-season was met with shock throughout English football, with the south coast club well on their way to staying up in their first season back in the Premier League after a seven-year absence.

    He again drew 0-0 in his first game of a managerial spell, with Southampton putting in a battling performance against an Everton side who, at the time, were outside contenders for Champions League qualification under David Moyes.

    (Photo by Ian Walton/Getty Images).

    This was Pochettino’s first time having a full summer to prepare for a managerial job rather than coming in mid-season, earning the Spurs gig off the back of his fine work at Southampton.

    The north Londoners survived a red card and a missed Mark Noble penalty before snatching all three points in stoppage time courtesy of an Eric Dier goal on what was also his first outing with Tottenham, who left the Boleyn Ground with a sweet win over their capital rivals.

    It was back to mid-season appointments for Pochettino six-and-a-half years later as he filled the vacancy left by Thomas Tuchel’s departure for Chelsea.

    He maintained his record of never losing his first game in charge of a club, but in truth this was two points dropped for PSG, who at the time were three points adrift of surprise Ligue 1 leaders Lyon. They also had to come from behind against an in-form Les Verts side.

    Sunday won’t be the first time that Liverpool provide the opposition for Pochettino in his first game in charge – the Reds also had that role when the Argentine began his reign as Chelsea boss three years ago.

    Once again he’d end with a draw, as an entertaining clash on the opening weekend of the Premier League season saw Luis Diaz’s opener for the visitors cancelled out by Axel Disasi as each team had a further goal disallowed.

    Four draws and a win for Pochettino from his managerial debuts at his previous clubs – it’s a respectable record, but not an overly intimidating one.

    According to recent reports, it feels more pertinent to look at his first results when taking charge mid-season, just as he’s doing now with Man United. All three of those games were drawn, and another such result on Sunday would be regarded as a decent start for him.

    It’d also represent disappointment for Liverpool, who are without an Anfield win over their arch-rivals in three attempts since the famous 7-0 romp in March 2023.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.
    • The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.
    • During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

    The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

    During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

    Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in upcoming manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

    Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

    It has been revealed that jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

    Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

    After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

    Sources indicate that newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

    The North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

    Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

    In a recent development, bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

    In a recent development, referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059.

    In a recent development, A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

    Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

    Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

    There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

    Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

    Sources indicate that chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

    Industry observers note that newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

    The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

    Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

    Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

    The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

    Newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

    Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

    It has been revealed that play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

    Sources indicate that time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

    Sources indicate that rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

    Recent findings suggest that leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

    Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

    Bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

    Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

    Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

    Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

    Corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

    Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

    Sources indicate that jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

    The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

    Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

    Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

    Recent findings suggest that newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

    Recent findings suggest that lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

    Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

    That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

    Good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

    Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

    It has been revealed that the game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

    In a recent development, bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

    Sources indicate that on the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

    Industry observers note that A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

    Sources indicate that leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a significant threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

    Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

    It has been revealed that newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

    Sources indicate that newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

    Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

    Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

    There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

    Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

    Fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

    Newcastle get the game under way.

    Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

    Sources indicate that the former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

    Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane.

    Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst.

    Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa.

    Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave.

    Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq.

    Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

    It has been revealed that upcoming manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

    “It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

    Industry observers note that “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

    According to recent reports, “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

    The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

    He remained tight-lipped about latest signings.

    According to recent reports, “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he mentioned.

    Industry observers note that “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

    Jaissle noted he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

    Sources indicate that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

    “The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Newly introduced York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team unveiled on Saturday.

    Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

    Sources indicate that prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

    Sources indicate that the 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

    According to recent reports, shesterkin was a substantial reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

    Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

    Upcoming York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

    In a recent development, first, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

    Industry observers note that upcoming York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

    According to recent reports, the one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a significant commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

    In a recent development, obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and Fresh York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

    In a recent development, however, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

    Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether Latest York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so promptly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of significant swings in recent history.

    Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

    📅 15 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2824 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
    • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
    • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

    Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

    His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

    Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

    Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

    United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

    United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

    Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

    But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

    Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

    In a recent development, AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

    Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

    That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand said everything you need to know about this moment...

    Aug 22: Hull City vs Manchester United.

    Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town.

    Sep 6: Everton vs Manchester United.

    Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City.

    Sep 20: Fulham vs Manchester United.

    It has been revealed that united’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

    Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

    Four minutes of added time to be played...

    United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

    For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

    Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

    More substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

    Big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

    Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

    Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

    Industry observers note that more changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

    Recent findings suggest that manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by fresh signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

    Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

    Wholesale changes on the hour mark...

    Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

    For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

    Milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

    United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

    Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

    Recent findings suggest that all square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

    Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

    Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

    De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

    It has been revealed that manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

    The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

    Sources indicate that santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

    Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

    Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs.

    United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

    Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

    Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

    United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

    In a recent development, A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

    Industry observers note that carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

    It has been revealed that A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

    Recent findings suggest that estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

    Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

    Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

    Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

    Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

    United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

    Industry observers note that szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

    The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely newly introduced cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

    We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

    Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

    Marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

    Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

    The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the newly introduced campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

    Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

    So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

    Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

    At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

    “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

    “I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

    “But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the significant ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

    According to recent reports, at the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri said Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

    Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

The star tight end is battling an ankle injury.
