    Justice Hill fumbled a ball at the goal line earlier in the game, and it went out the back of the end zone for the touchback.

    In a recent development, hill made up for it later in the second half. He ran down the left sideline, stayed in bounds, and held onto the ball. Hill scored the 19-yard TD to put the Ravens up 26-22.

    Pittsburgh came into today's game with a 6-3 record and in contention for the AFC North lead, while Philadelphia is riding a seven-game losing streak.

    The first half was all Eagles, though. Philadelphia heads into halftime with a 13-3 led as Pittsburgh could only muster a field goal.

    Despite dealing with knee and ankle injuries, the Jaguars are expected to give running back Bhayshul Tuten the "bulk of carries" in Week 11, per CBS reporter Tracy Wolfson.

    Tuten's practice reps have been limited as he works through the injuries, logging limited sessions on Wednesday and Friday while sitting out of Thursday's practice. He was left without any official designation on the final injury report.

    It has been revealed that tuten is the team's leading rusher with 609 yards and five touchdowns this season, adding another 206 yards and three scores through the air. Chris Rodriguez is his backup.

    Industry observers note that buffalo finally had a possession not go its way. Josh Allen had his pass batted and a Miami rookie linebacker made the leap to come down with the deflection for the turnover.

    Industry observers note that newly introduced Orleans has picked off Caleb Williams for the second time today. Williams had a pass tipped at the line and it went into the air and came down right into the waiting arms of a Saints defender for the turnover.

    Baker Mayfield and wide receiver Ted Hurst III combined to get Tampa Bay on the board. Mayfield found his receiver for the 23-yard score as Hurst made an impressive contested catch.

    Industry observers note that the Panthers offense continues to click against the Ravens. Quarterback Bryce Young found Tet McMillan over the middle for the 7-yard score.

    Dallas' Massive 3 has each found the end zone now. After Javonte Williams and CeeDee Lamb had already scored, George Pickens finally got his.

    Dak Prescott threw the ball over the middle and found Pickens for the 10-yard score.

    Recent findings suggest that dallas' defensive strategy may just be to score a TD on every possession and hope that is enough. At the moment, on Sunday, it is as the Cowboys lead 27-6 with just over four minutes left in the first half.

    The Saints got a little cute at the goal line. On second and goal from the 1-yard line, Tyler Shough went with a play action and the play was a failure as he just had to get rid of it with defenders bearing down on him.

    On third down, Shough again went to pass, but this time got it quickly to veteran RB Alvin Kamara who came down with it and barely stayed in bounds for the score.

    The Bills offense had no trouble getting down the field against the Dolphins' defense. Buffalo had second and goal from the 1-yard line and running back James Cook bulldozed his way into the end zone.

    Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce had already connected for a TD against the Cardinals, but they were determined that wasn't enough.

    The future Hall of Fame duo teamed up for another touchdown, this one from 22 yards out.

    This may be one to turn your TVs to if you can even if the matchup isn't exciting on paper.

    After the Ravens muffed a punt and Chuba Hubbard scored a TD two plays later, the Panthers were kicking off.

    Baltimore returner Devontez Walker, a Charlotte, North Carolina native, returned the kickoff 84 yards for the touchdown.

    It looked like Chicago was going to get set up with a fresh set of downs in the red zone. Caleb Williams swung a pass to tight end Colston Loveland who ran down the sideline, picking up good yardage.

    Just when it looked like a Saints defender was going to tackle him, but instead Loveland hurdled the defender, regained his balance and made it into the end zone for the score.

    Tennessee ran six plays and picked up only 18 yards, but it was enough to get into field goal range.

    Titans running back Tony Pollard picked up 19 yards on three carries, but a sack and an incompletion brought up fourth-and-eight on the Dallas 30.

    Sources indicate that joey Slye came out for the 48-yard field goal attempt and nailed it. Tennessee trails 20-6 with 10:34 left in the first half.

    What else is going to happen in this game?

    With 10 minutes left in the first half we have already seen a safety, both teams pull off trick plays for a TD, and there was a fumble out of the back of the end zone for a turnover.

    Now, Carolina was punting it away and Baltimore's returned muffed the punt and the Panthers recovered.

    Carolina wasted little time making them pay for it as two plays later, running back Chuba Hubbard took off for the 18-yard score.

    All of a sudden the Panthers lead this one 14-12.

    The Chicago defense picked up its second turnover of the game against Newly introduced Orleans.

    Saints QB Tyler Shough was rolling right and tried to throw on the run. It was snatched out of the air by Bears rookie Dillon Thieneman.

    According to recent reports, there is "not a lot of optimism" that Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers will play in Week 11, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. Bowers is dealing with ankle and quad injuries. Bowers logged limited practices on Thursday and Friday and is still "pushing to play" even though his status is looking grim.

    Bowers exited with an ankle injury in Week 10's loss to the Seattle Seahawks, though head coach Klint Kubiak labeled him "day-to-day" and remarked the injury wasn't as bad as initially feared.

    It's a tough blow, particularly for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who is making his second career start in Week 11 against the Denver Broncos. Mendoza completed 17 of 29 pass attempts for 143 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions in his debut as a starter last week.

    Ravens running back Justice Hill was barreling toward the end zone at the end of a long run.

    Hill picked up 36 yards, but didn't get the last one necessary for the score. Instead, the Panthers defender punched the ball out of Hill's hands and it went out the back of the end zone.

    This resulted, by rule, in a touchback for the Panthers.

    According to recent reports, the Bears offense got into the redzone. Quarterback Caleb Williams waited for the play to develop and then flipped a shovel pass to D'Andre Swift as the running back walked in for the score.

    It looked like Dak Prescott was throwing the ball away under pressure from the Tennessee defense.

    Prescott was rolling right and just barely got the pass off. It looked destined for out of bounds, but then CeeDee Lamb came into frame and the pass was perfectly placed for Lamb to not only grab it, but also get the necessary two feet in for the score.

    Sunday's matchup between the Tennessee Titans and the Dallas Cowboys looks poised for high-scoring madness, as the two worst defenses in the league face off.

    Dallas and Tennessee are one-two in total offensive yards allowed this season, with both defenses boasting more than 3,900 yards allowed by opponents. But while the Cowboys' offense has been able to salvage a 4-6 record, the Titans are 1-8, with just a surprisingly good offensive line holding the team together.

    Dallas tried to reset the concern by stripping first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties, and having senior defensive assistant and veteran coach Mike Pettine call the plays going forward.

    Tennessee, meanwhile, appears to be actively tanking. But the team did opt to keep star running back Tony Pollard, who should provide some offensive entertainment against a Cowboys defense that, in the words of their own head coach, "tackled like s***" last week.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Titans face the Cowboys in Week 11, airing on Fox.

    Dallas' Significant 3 has each found the end zone now. After Javonte Williams and CeeDee Lamb had already scored, George Pickens finally got his.

    Dak Prescott threw the ball over the middle and found Pickens for the 10-yard score.

    In a recent development, dallas' defensive strategy may just be to score a TD on every possession and hope that is enough. Currently, on Sunday, it is as the Cowboys lead 27-6 with just over four minutes left in the first half.

    Tennessee ran six plays and picked up only 18 yards, but it was enough to get into field goal range.

    Titans running back Tony Pollard picked up 19 yards on three carries, but a sack and an incompletion brought up fourth-and-eight on the Dallas 30.

    Joey Slye came out for the 48-yard field goal attempt and nailed it. Tennessee trails 20-6 with 10:34 left in the first half.

    It looked like Dak Prescott was throwing the ball away under pressure from the Tennessee defense.

    Prescott was rolling right and just barely got the pass off. It looked destined for out of bounds, but then CeeDee Lamb came into frame and the pass was perfectly placed for Lamb to not only grab it, but also get the necessary two feet in for the score.

    Tennessee's offense was clicking on its first possession of the game, but not the second.

    The Titans had a five-yard run on first down, lost a yard on a Carnell Tate reeption on second down and then Cam Ward was sacked by Justin Houston on third down.

    The quarter ended, but when the second quarter starts, the Titans will be punting.

    While the Dallas defense has struggled, the offense is firing on all cylinders. The Cowboys picked up 74 yards on six plays, including a touchdown run by wide receiver KaVontae Turpin.

    The speedster showed off his wheels and went around the left end for a 22-yard score.

    It has been revealed that dallas didn't go for 2 this time and just let Brandon Aubrey knock through the extra point. The Cowboys lead 13-3.

    One of the main stories this week was Dallas DC Christian Parker losing play-calling duties to Mike Pettine while remaining the DC.

    Dallas' defense went with a bend-don't-break approach on Tennessee's first drive of the game.

    It has been revealed that cam Ward hit Chimere Dike for a 22-yard gain, then later had an 8-yard reception. Running back Tony Pollard picked up 13 on a carry.

    The Titans got into the redzone but were unable to find the end zone. Instead, Joey Slye knocked through a 38-yard field goal to make it 6-3, with the Cowboys in front.

    Tennessee's challenge of the first down was not successful.

    Dallas got the fresh set of downs and ran Javonte Williams twice. On the second attempt, the running back forced his way into the end zone for the score.

    The Cowboys opted to go for two because of a penalty giving them a closer attempt, but it failed.

    Dallas has been grooving its way down the field against Tennessee.

    Facing fourth and short, the Cowboys kept the offense on the field and went for it. Quarterback Dak Prescott kept the ball for a quarterback keeper, and it looked on the broadcast that he had easily gotten it.

    Tennessee head coach Robert Saleh wasn't convinced, though, and tossed an early challenge flag. The ruling was upheld — first down, Cowboys.

    Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate will return to the active lineup for Tennessee in Week 11, officially active for the first time since Week 7 after dealing with a shoulder injury.

    Despite having missed two games, Tate leads the team with 413 receiving yards this year with a single receiving touchdown. His presence will be key this week, especially after teammate Wan'Dale Robinson was placed on season-ending injured reserve with an ankle injury this week.

    Here's a look at the full list of inactives for Titans-Cowboys in Week 11.

    Christian Parker's job as Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator is safe for now, but he will no longer be calling the plays, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said on Wednesday.

    Mike Pettine, who was added last month as a senior defensive assistant to support Parker, will have play-calling responsibilities going forward.

    "A different perspective [will be] good for us," Schottenheimer noted. "Play-calling is a very collaborative thing.".

    According to recent reports, the decision comes after another poor showing by the Dallas defense during Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. After the game, head coach Brian Schottenheimer didn't exactly show support for the 34-year-old Parker, who was hired in the offseason after two seasons on Nick Sirianni's staff with the Philadelphia Eagles.

    "At the end of the day, we tackled like s**t in the second half," Scottenheimer said after the 49ers recorded 584 yards of offense, the most the Cowboys have allowed at home in franchise history.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has won the 2026 American League MVP, the BBWAA announced Thursday night.
    • It has been revealed that the Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing AL teams.
    • It has been revealed that alvarez, 29, bounced back from an injury-riddled disaster in 2025, during which he only played in 48 games.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has won the 2026 American League MVP, the BBWAA announced Thursday night.

    It has been revealed that the Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing AL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

    It has been revealed that alvarez, 29, bounced back from an injury-riddled disaster in 2025, during which he only played in 48 games. This time around, he avoided the IL and appeared in 158 games. He hit .316/.432/.601 (190 OPS+) with 34 doubles, a triple, 42 home runs, 106 RBI, 105 runs and 6.8 WAR. He made a late run at the Triple Crown, missing out by one home run and seven RBI. He did lead the majors in all three triple slash categories, though, leading in average by five points, on-base percentage by a whopping 42 points -- he led the majors in walks -- and 31 points in slugging percentage. Add the latter two and his OPS victory was 90 points -- 1.033 to second place's .943 (National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong).

    The only players in MLB history to lead the majors in all three triple slash categories:.

    Alvarez becomes just the third Astros player to win MVP after Jeff Bagwell in 1994 and Jose Altuve in 2017.

    Rays third baseman Junior Caminero finished in second. At age 22, he played all 162 games, leading the Rays to the best AL record. He hit .276/.360/.524 (144 OPS+) with 42 home runs, 101 RBI and 100 runs, posting a 5.7 WAR. He's already made history, too, as the Rays had previously never had a player finish in the top five of MVP voting.

    Royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. came in third. This is now his fourth straight season in the top seven and third straight season in the top four. He finished second in 2024. This season, he hit .281/.359/.441 (125 OPS+) with 33 doubles, 18 homers, 54 RBI, 94 runs, 45 steals and 6.7 WAR.

    It has been revealed that the Las Vegas Raiders and Denver Broncos will face off for the first time this season in Week 11's afternoon window, with kickoff set for 4:25 p.m. ET at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver.

    Industry observers note that after starting the season 3-0, the Raiders have been on a slide, going 1-6 over their past seven games. No. 1 overall pick rookie Fernando Mendoza is set to make his second career start following the trade of Kirk Cousins ahead of the deadline this week, up against another challenging defense after facing the Seattle Seahawks in Week 11. All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers is questionable for this matchup, which could leave Mendoza without his top receiving option.

    The Broncos entered the week tied with the Kansas City Chiefs for the best record in the AFC West at 7-2. They're 10.5-point home favorites in this contest and are on a five-game winning streak coming off the Week 10 bye. That win streak began as head coach Sean Payton resumed offensive play-calling from OC Davis Webb after a slow start on offense.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Raiders face the Broncos in Week 11, airing on CBS.

    It has been revealed that there is "not a lot of optimism" that Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers will play in Week 11, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. Bowers is dealing with ankle and quad injuries. Bowers logged limited practices on Thursday and Friday and is still "pushing to play" even though his status is looking grim.

    Bowers exited with an ankle injury in Week 10's loss to the Seattle Seahawks, though head coach Klint Kubiak labeled him "day-to-day" and mentioned the injury wasn't as bad as initially feared.

    It's a tough blow, particularly for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who is making his second career start in Week 11 against the Denver Broncos. Mendoza completed 17 of 29 pass attempts for 143 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions in his debut as a starter last week.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    In a recent development, that made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    Sources indicate that loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    According to recent reports, our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Sources indicate that steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    According to recent reports, finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an concern is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the National League MVP award for the 2026 season unanimously, the BBWAA revealed Thursday evening.
    • The Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing NL teams.
    • Though the results were unsurprising by the time the year wound down, going back to the start of the season, this marks a huge upset.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the National League MVP award for the 2026 season unanimously, the BBWAA revealed Thursday evening.

    The Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing NL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

    Though the results were unsurprising by the time the year wound down, going back to the start of the season, this marks a huge upset. Shohei Ohtani was the overwhelming favorite to win the award heading into the season and maintained favorite status through the All-Star break. A combination of his injuries and PCA's monster season turned the tide late.

    Appearing in all 162 games, Crow-Armstrong hit .280/.372/.570 (156 OPS+) with 31 doubles, eight triples, 45 home runs, 107 RBI, 119 runs, 41 steals and 9.8 WAR. He led the majors in WAR, runs, home runs and total bases while leading the NL in slugging, OPS and OPS+. He became the seventh player in MLB history to join the 40-40 club (40 home runs and 40 steals in the same season). Further, he led the majors in multiple advanced defensive metrics, putting together one of the great all-around seasons from a position player in recent memory.

    PCA joins the following list of Cubs to win MVP:.

    Ohtani, the four-time MVP, finishes in second. At the plate, Ohtani hit .275/.377/.512 with 26 doubles, four triples, 30 home runs, 81 RBI, 89 runs, 11 steals and 3.2 WAR. On the mound, he was 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 95 strikeouts in 85 ⅔ innings with 3.2 WAR.

    The nationally underrated Brewers second baseman Brice Turang finishes in third. He still hasn't made an All-Star Game, though he did start 2026 as a member of Team USA in the World Baseball Classic. In the regular season, Turang hit .268/.366/.450 (124 OPS+) with 37 doubles, three triples, 21 home runs, 100 RBI, 102 runs and 7.3 WAR, rating out as one of the best defenders in baseball.

    #61923. Now with an MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong is on the path for an all-time great career. Where could he stack up?

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1111 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Now with an MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong is on the path for an all-time great career. Where could he stack up?

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1111 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.
    • Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors.
    • To answer that, we'll look backwards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.

    Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors. He hit .280/.372/.570 with stellar defense, led the league in home runs (tied with Kyle Schwarber) and massively upgraded his on-base skills. Now, just a few months shy of his 25th birthday, he has an MVP to his name.

    So what's next? To answer that, we'll look backwards.

    Since integration, only eight center fielders have posted at least 8.0 WAR in a season age-25 or younger: Willie Mays, Mickey Mantle, Willie Davis, César Cedeño, Ken Griffey Jr., Andruw Jones, Mike Trout and PCA. The only ones to top PCA's 9.8 were Mays, Mantle and Trout. If we went back to pre-integration, Tris Speaker and Ty Cobb were the only others who bested PCA here.

    What road map will PCA's career follow?

    Willie Davis was an inconsistent hitter through his age-23 season but had flashed a nice power-speed combo. Sound familiar? That gaudy 8.4 WAR total in 1964, though, was driven largely by monster defensive metrics. Davis hit .294/.316/.413 (110 OPS+) with 23 doubles, seven triples, 12 home runs, 77 RBI, 91 runs and 42 steals. There's little doubt that PCA's 2026 season dwarfed this one overall, and Davis was far behind Mays (11.0) for the league lead in WAR.

    For the rest of his career, Davis averaged 3.1 WAR per season, and though he had good years, he never reached 6.0 WAR again. The WAR figure was, again, mostly driven by defense. He had several good offensive seasons, but his only 20-homer season came in 1962 when he was 22, two years prior to his career year.

    Davis' career probably looks a lot like PCA's apparent upside before his home run barrage in the first half of 2025. He racked up over 60 career WAR with a decent batting average, excellent defense and excellent baserunning.

    With PCA reaching 30-30 last year and 40-40 this year, though, the bar has been raised.

    César Cedeño followed up his 8.0 WAR season with a 7.4 season at age 22 and 5.8 at age 23. He was very good through age 29 and, in fact, the most statistically similar player through both ages 27 and 28 was Hall of Famer Carl Yastrzemski. Things fell apart after that. As a quick and easy way to illustrate it, Cedeño amassed 49.4 WAR through his age-29 season and only 3.6 in his final six years.

    Sources indicate that it's easier to remember that Andruw Jones' career unfolded in similar fashion because we witnessed it not too long ago and then discussed his Hall of Fame candidacy during his nine turns on the ballot before he finally made it in. In Jones' 12 Braves' season, he racked up 368 home runs, 1,117 RBI and 61 WAR while generally being considered the best defensive center fielder in baseball. Once he left, in time for his age-31 season, Jones accrued just 1.7 WAR in his last five seasons.

    Through Jones' age-28 season, the most statistically similar players are Bryce Harper and Frank Robinson.

    To compare these two to Crow-Armstrong, the argument would be that he'll continue to look like one of the best players in baseball -- even if taking steps backward from being the very best in the 2026 regular season -- before falling apart once he's around 30 years old.

    Recent findings suggest that certainly possible, but given the adjustments he's already not only been willing to make at the plate, but eager to make, I'm just not seeing him all of a sudden hitting a wall. Sure, at some point he'll start losing speed and that'll affect his defensive range and baserunning, but why would the plate skills deteriorate all of a sudden?

    Then again, few saw it coming with Jones.

    All three of these players were on the path to having an argument as the best player in history before injuries derailed them in their 30s and left them as mere "all-time greats.".

    Through Mickey Mantle's age-30 season, he had 90.7 WAR. He averaged 121 games per year in his final six seasons, putting up 19.5 WAR. Through  Ken Griffey Jr.'s age-30 season, he had 76.2 WAR. He played 10 more seasons, but only amassed 7.6 more WAR. Through Mike Trout's age-27 season, he had 72.1 WAR (his top statistical similars were Mantle, Robinson and Griffey). We'll skip 2020 for obvious reasons, but since then he's averaged 90 games and 3.0 WAR per season.

    Sources indicate that even with the drop-offs, it would be surprising to see Crow-Armstrong reach this level because it's surprising to see any player reach this lofty standard. In career WAR among center fielders, Mantle is fourth, Trout is fifth and Griffey is sixth. They trail only Cobb, Speaker and the guy we're going to discuss next. Joe DiMaggio is seventh.

    Despite the lofty standard PCA set for himself in 2026, coming close to Willie Mays' career would be jaw-droppingly shocking, and that is absolutely not intended as a slight.

    Sources indicate that mays has an argument as the greatest player in baseball history and he put himself in that discussion by being good at everything and doing it all with great longevity. From his age-23 to -35 seasons, he led the majors in WAR eight times, leading the NL an additional two times. His worst seasons in that timeframe were 7.6 and 7.8 WAR. In that span, he also led the league in runs twice, hits once, triples three times, home runs three times, stolen bases four times, average once, on-base percentage once, slugging percentage five times and OPS five times.

    According to recent reports, mays even posted 5.2 WAR at age 39 and 6.3 at age 40. He led the NL with a .425 OBP when he was 40 years old! He hit .345/.411/.667 at age 23.

    Mays' 156.2 career WAR ranks third among position players all-time behind two guys you might have heard of: Barry Bonds (162.8) and Babe Ruth (162.3).

    I feel pretty strongly Pete Crow-Armstrong isn't headed for a run at this career and that's just fine.

    In a recent development, the realistic long-term range for the 2026 National League MVP seems somewhere between Cedeño and Mantle. It's a wide variance of outcomes between those two, obviously, as well it should be when the player we discuss is only 24 years old. For his name to be mentioned among these at all is a testament to the year Crow-Armstrong just put together.

    Industry News: MLB rumors: Rangers in mix for Sato, Dodgers seek infield help, Korean slugger could join free agent class

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the annual GM Meetings came and went this week with only one significant transaction: Evan Phillips signed with the Braves.
    • Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors -- A LOT of rumors -- and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason.
    • The Rangers are among the teams with interest in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports The Athletic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the annual GM Meetings came and went this week with only one significant transaction: Evan Phillips signed with the Braves. Phillips, our 34th-ranked free agent, received a three-year deal worth $35 million. He'll replace Raisel Iglesias in Atlanta's bullpen and pair with Robert Suarez at the end of the game. The Braves could still re-sign Iglesias too, I suppose.

    Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors -- A LOT of rumors -- and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the crucial offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Friday's hot stove happenings.

    The Rangers are among the teams with interest in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports The Athletic. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers, though he does not stand out defensively, and could land at first base or in the corner outfield in MLB. Texas could stand to upgrade at first base and could always slot Sato in at DH as well.

    We ranked Sato as the fourth-best free agent available and the best free agent position player. The reigning Triple Crown winner in Japan hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs in 2026. Sato, 28 in March, has some similarities to Munetaka Murakami as a lefty with big power and swing-and-miss concerns, though Sato is a much more aggressive hitter and won't walk as much as Murakami.

    With Miguel Rojas retired, the Dodgers are looking to add a right-handed hitting infielder, according to The Athletic. Mookie Betts and Max Muncy are entrenched on the left side of the infield. Tommy Edman, a switch-hitter, is penciled in at second base, with fellow switch-hitter Alex Freeland next in line as depth. Freeland has not hit much in his limited MLB time, however.

    This is not a great free agent class overall, but it does feature several utility infielders who hit right-handed. Among them are Mauricio Dubón, Ha-Seong Kim, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, and Edmundo Sosa. Glovemen Oswald Peraza (Angels) and Jared Triolo (Pirates) are potential trade targets. Rojas was a very productive role player for Los Angeles. He won't be so easy to replace.

    The Padres are receiving calls about catchers Luis Campusano and Freddy Fermin, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. Top prospect Ethan Salas was called up in September and became the youngest catcher to appear in the postseason in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series. Salas is the future behind the plate, making Campusano or Fermin (or perhaps both) expendable.

    In a recent development, campusano and Fermin are very different players. Campusano is a bat-first catcher who might be worth keeping given his age (28) and the fact that the Padres could slot him at DH. That stated, those same qualities make him appealing to other teams. Fermin, 31, is a terrific defender who hasn't hit much the last few years. The Padres need pitching and could deal a catcher or two for an arm or two.

    Samsung Lions outfielder Ja-Wook Koo has hired a upcoming agent and is looking to make the jump to MLB, reports MLB.com. Koo, a 10-time All-Star and this year's Korean Series MVP, has been among the best hitters in the Korea Baseball Organization the last few years. The 33-year-old hit .371/.458/.581 with 15 homers and nearly as many walks (66) as strikeouts (71) in 2026.

    Koo's age and the fact he's a left-handed hitter in a market inundated with left-handed hitting outfielders will work against him in free agency. He has a great track record in Korea, though, including a history of high contact rates, which could make him a cheaper and more appealing target than MLB free agents like Michael Conforto, Trent Grisham, Cedric Mullins, and Daulton Varsho.

    Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

    📅 16 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5971 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
    • In a recent development, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
    • It has been revealed that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the latest signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    In a recent development, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    It has been revealed that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    Recent findings suggest that first Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    Industry observers note that another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    “They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    Industry observers note that “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    In a recent development, you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

    When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

    It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

    City, in contrast to their opponents, indicated a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where upcoming boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

    In a recent development, throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

    Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

    Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    According to recent reports, had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal indicated was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

    “I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

    You would be brave to say it will be their last.

    Arsenal (4-2-3-1) Raya 7; White 7, Mosquera 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie h-t): Guimarães 7 (Rice h-t), Lewis-Skelly 8 (Zublimendi 75); Madueke 6 [Saka 60], Odegaard 8 (Eze 84), Tzolis 7; Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 75). Booked Calafiori, Odegaard. Subs Kepa (g), Merino, Dowman.

    Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

    Manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

    Referee Sam Barrott (Yorkshire).

    In a recent development, it’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

    Recent findings suggest that I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

    Recent findings suggest that A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we highlighted, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

    He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

    It has been revealed that I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

    Sources indicate that the feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

    Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

    Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka.

    According to recent reports, the players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

    Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7.

    What happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

    Recent findings suggest that we played some brilliant football. Great performance and a great way to start the season.

    I always want to help the team as much possible with goals and assists. I want to score more goals.

    We showed our level today. We’re showed we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again.

    We want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again.

    According to recent reports, the league champions kick-off the domestic season with a resounding and stylish victory. Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.

    Marmoush is feeling his hip after a challenge by Mosquera. City have a free-kick wide right. Gabriel heads away Grealish’s delivery in trademark fashion.

    Just three minutes of added time to play. No City player is there to meet Cherki’s low cross and White can clear under little pressure.

    Rice uncharacteristically caught dallying in midfield but City cannot capitalise. Cheers from the Arsenal fans as Saka wins a throw in from Grealish. Marmoush with a chance to run at Mosquera, but his touch is far too heavy.

    City have a free-kick in a crossing position right of centre, but many of their fans are now packing up their banners and heading for the exits. If they haven’t already. Cherki’s delivery is poor, and Rice heads away.

    In a recent development, odegaard with a loose touch, and a yellow card for catching Grealish with the resulting challenge. That was the Arsenal captain’s last action of the game, he is replaced by Eberechi Eze. Odegaard has looked back to his 2024 past today, Eze’s best chance of a start might be from the left.

    According to recent reports, city’s best move of the second half: Cherki gliding through the challenges and finding Semenyo with a lovely reverse pass, and his shot was drilled towards the far corner. Sharp reflexes by Raya to plunge to his right and save.

    Nico Gonzalez replaces Kovacic as Maresca makes his sixth change of the second half. The game has felt like a training exercise since Odegaard’s third goal with the occasional flash of quality.

    Chance for Saka! Cracking low cross from Hincapie, but Saka sweeps over from near the penalty spot. Too much on it as he tried to help the ball on its way.

    Recent findings suggest that better tempo to Manchester City’s football, and Gvardiol has gone down holding his face in the box. It was more of a shoulder to shoulder with White, and the incident is checked and cleared by VAR.

    Here come two more Arsenal changes: Havertz and Lewis-Skelly deserve their ovation, replaced by Gyokeres and Zubimendi.

    In a recent development, chance for Tzolis to play Saka clean through on goal but he delayed a fraction and Gvardiol got back in to defend. It was a great flick on by Havertz to free Tzolis. Gyokeres is ready to replace the German.

    Cherki with a shot from distance, saved by Raya. That was City’s first shot on target of the second half.

    Odegaard with a disguised ball through to White, who may have been offside, and Tzolis is close to applying the touch that would have made it four. Feels like the game is meandering towards its conclusion.

    Recent findings suggest that arsenal back themselves to play out from a tight spot again, but Semenyo does well to force Hincapie to concede a throw in. Arsenal then soak up another spell of City possession, they have been so much more compact defensively than Maresca’s team. Whenever Arsenal have the ball in City’s half they look dangerous, whereas City’s possession has been sterile.

    In a recent development, city chasing shadows when Arsenal play out from the back. Arsenal moving the ball with great assurance, but you suspect everyone has an extra yard of space than they would find in a full-throttle Premier League game.

    Semenyo gave Hincapie a tough time in the League Cup final in March, and was not shy in boasting about it after the game. I suspect Hincapie is a defender who keeps a little black book of those who have crossed him.

    It has been revealed that lovely moment in midfield from Odegaard, letting the ball run across his box and pushing it beyond Rico Lewis. Saka in acres on the far side after he outmuscles Gvardiol, but he shoots into the side netting. Tried to give Donnarumma the eyes.

    City with a spell of possession in the Arsenal half, and Gvardiol glances a header over the bar from a very decent Grealish cross. Arsenal hard to break down once they are in that 4-4-2 shape.

    Here come the changes: Foden and Anderson off, Cherki and Rico Lewis on.

    In a recent development, arsenal subs: Saka and Hincapue on for Calafiori and Madueke. Saka has braids this seasons, so a new look.

    According to recent reports, arsenal popping the ball around in the sunshine now, to olés from their fans. Maresca is about to make two more changes, so five subs before the hour tells you were City are physically. Saka is going to come on for Arsenal.

    Gvardiol booked, and here come more City changes, this is a fitness exercise for Maresca now. Haaland and O’Reilly off, Marmoush and Guehi on. Arteta will surely reply in kind around the hour mark.

    That really should be game over now, but given the loosey-goosey nature of these games I suppose you never know. I think the only way this fixture can matter is if one team takes a battering, and there’s a risk of that for City now.

    Christos Tzolis registered 29 assists in 52 competitive games for Club Brugge last season. He’s on two assists in 48 competitive minutes for Arsenal.

    What composure from the Arsenal captain, running into the box untracked and sitting down first Gvardiol then Donnarumma before finding the empty net. It is clever play from Tzolis, finding Odegaard with the pass for his second assist of the game. The run from Calafiori was crucial to pull City’s defence out of shape.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    Man City kick off in the second 45 minutes. These matches tend to lose their rhythm in the second half.

    So far, Manchester City’s first glimpse of life after Pep Guardiola is inauspicious. Enzo Maresca might be his predecessor’s doppelgänger, but his attempt to emulate the same style has proved abortive: plenty of possession, but minimal impact. It smacks of desperation that Jack Grealish is being thrown in at half-time, his first appearance for the club for 15 months.

    Sources indicate that looks like a pre-planned change from Manchester City and Arsenal: Jack Grealish makes an unlikely comeback, replacing Doku, and Declan Rice replaces Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal’s two massive hitters in midfield sharing the game.

    7 - Kai Havertz has been involved in more goals against Manchester City (7 - 4 goals, 3 assists) than against any other side in his club career. Occasion. pic.twitter.com/ln7PQnjboJ.

    Advantage Arsenal at half time, and they have looked a sharper, more cohesive team. City have had plenty of possession, but much of it was sterile until that late flurry when Raya saved from Haaland and White blocked Doku’s shot. The first 45 minutes will have ticked all of the boxes for Arteta: there has been some strong penalty box defending, some flowing moves from back to front and two well-taken goals.

    Flimsy defending from City again, Havertz finding it easy to run to the byline, and the ball is cleared off the line after Odegaard poked the ball towards goal after a Donnarumma parry.

    “You’re getting sacked in the morning,” sing the Arsenal fans at Maresca as the whistle blows.

    Industry observers note that mosquera defends well against Doku at the expense of a corner, which Raya claims with ease. There is going to be just one minute of added time.

The winger is such an outlet for his team, but the final decision is lacking too often, which is not a novel observation.

    Madueke then finds White on the overlap, he chips the ball to the back post where Calafiori is free and he volleys over.

Raya saved after Haaland was picked out by Doku, with Lewis-Skelly defending well to deny a rebound, before Semenyo picks out Doku with a lofted cross, but White through himself in front of the volley and made a crucial block.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    Ben White thought he had nipped in front of Doku to intercept a straight Kovacic pass, but the referee blows for a foul against the Arsenal man.

    Recent findings suggest that then Haaland has a sight of goal for the first time: a peeling run into the right channel, found by Doku, but it was tough angle on his weaker foot. Scooped it over the bar.

    In a recent development, foden takes up a lovely position behind the Arsenal midfield, but his through ball towards Haaland hits Gabriel on the back of the heel. Then Semenyo wins a corner in a joust with Calafiori. Referee blows for some pushing and shoving.

    Industry observers note that eventually the corner is taken, cleared initially, before teasing Foden cross drifts beyond the back post. Foden the pick of the bunch for City, which is unsurprising considering he has a full pre-season behind him.

    It has been revealed that the Arsenal supporters are really, really enjoying this. They’re “doing the Poznan” to mock the City fans.

    Industry observers note that an ideal outing for Arsenal, so far though it can be easy to over-index these games when players are not fully match fit. But Arteta will be pleased with the fluency in the passing through midfield, which was lacking at times last season.

    Christos Tzolis was signed to provide goals and assists, and he’s been doing so throughout pre-season. The Greek winger is perhaps more aggressive in his positioning than Leandro Trossard, the man he has replaced in the squad, and he was in the right place there to pick out Kai Havertz.

    The new signing Tzolis is involved with a clever header back across the six-yard box, the left winger was picked out by an inswinging Odegaard cross to the back post. Havertz rose above Dias, and his header down into the turf squeezed beyond Donnarumma. The ball bounced in off the back of the goalkeeper, could well be an own goal.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Houston Rockets improved to 11-3 on the season with a 147-119 beatdown of the Washington Wizards on Sunday night.

    While Houston is no stranger to an offensive explosion, ranking second in the NBA this season in offensive rating (121.2), the 147 points scored on Sunday were 12 more than they've scored in a game this season. It was a balanced scoring effort as a team, as six players reached double figures and three scored at least 25 points -- including Tari Eason off the bench.

    It has been revealed that that 25-point performance represents a upcoming season high for Eason -- his previous best was a 19-point effort against the Hawks -- as he went 10 for 14 from the field and 3 of 5 from 3-point range in 30 minutes off the bench. That effort earned Eason the honor of the walk-off TV interview, during which he gave a brutally honest (and hilarious) answer for why he was able to set a new season high and do so efficiently.

    Industry observers note that "Shit, the Wizards, for real. It was them," Eason remarked.

    Tari Eason on what allowed him to have a season-high 25 points off the bench tonight:"Shit, the Wizards, for real." pic.twitter.com/t4bOwtzw5r.

    A+ work here, no notes. Eason could've puffed out his chest after beating up on the Wizards or complimented his teammates for allowing him to get in a rhythm, but instead chose the honest route rarely taken by players in a post-game interview and simply admitted that anyone could get buckets on Washington.

    The Wizards are not the worst defense in the NBA -- that honor belongs to the Chicago Bulls -- but they are 25th in defensive rating and certainly do not boast very many elite defenders. Clearly, Eason didn't feel like he was doing anything special or out of the ordinary on Sunday night on his way to 25 points off the bench, and gave credit where it was due to the other team.

    Unfortunately for the Wizards, it is not credit they'd like to take, and this feels like the kind of (earned) disrespect that should light some kind of fire under Washington.

    #61915. Could Tarik Skubal take a short-term, high-AAV contract? Breaking down pros and cons

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Could Tarik Skubal take a short-term, high-AAV contract? Breaking down pros and cons

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (900 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m.
    • Skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly.
    • Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Barring a surprise agreement, the owners are almost certain to lock out the players at that time. Skubal is expected to sign before then.

    Skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly. There's a real chance Skubal signs a contract worth more than $400 million in the next two weeks or so. Excluding Shohei Ohtani, who is technically a pitcher but is really a two-way player, here are the largest pitching contracts in history:.

    1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    Industry observers note that 3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    According to recent reports, 3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    Recent findings suggest that something like, say, eight years at $50 million a year would give Skubal a $400 million contract that obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee and average annual value. Several major-market clubs are noted to be pursuing Skubal (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), who is a special free agent as an in-his-prime ace. Conditions are ripe for a record deal.

    There is also a chance Skubal goes the Valdez route, or the Bo Bichette/Kyle Tucker route, and signs a short-term contract with a high annual salary. It might only be a small chance, but there is a chance. The Athletic reports the Dodgers prefer such an arrangement with Skubal. ESPN notes Skubal has no interest in such a deal, though minds can always be changed.

    Recent findings suggest that with that in mind, here are the pros and cons of a high-dollar, short-term contract for Skubal. Keep in mind that such a contract is usually a three- or four-year deal with opt outs, not a straight one- or two-year contract, and Skubal wouldn't necessarily have to use the opt outs to re-enter free agency. He could leverage them into a new contract to stay with his team.

    1. Maximize earnings. Plain and simple, a short-term contract would give Skubal a chance to max out his earnings by making free agency available to him again as soon as next offseason. Go out, have a typical Skubal season in 2027, and perhaps market forces push the demand even higher than it is right now. Remember that, along with a salary cap, there could be a salary floor in the future. Small-market contenders like, say, the Guardians or Rays could throw many millions at Skubal to reach the floor in the future.

    Sources indicate that 2. Chance to set more records. This ties back to the last point. Skubal already set a newly introduced salary record for an arbitration-eligible player ($32 million in 2026) and he's positioned to set a new standard for pitcher contracts this offseason. Go back into free agency in a year or two, and Skubal (and Boras) could have a chance to break his own pitcher contract record. The record itself won't be a driving factor in that decision (the money will ultimately decide things), but it would be a nice feather in his cap.

    3. Freedom to change teams. Sometimes things don't work out. I don't think Juan Soto expected to miss the postseason in the first two years of his record 15-year, $765 million contract with the Mets. It's entirely possible Skubal could find his next situation not to his liking for whatever reason. Maybe the team doesn't contend, maybe he clashes with the coaching staff, maybe he doesn't like the local breakfast taco options. There could be a million different reasons it doesn't work. A short-term, high-dollar deal would give Skubal an escape hatch and allow him to head elsewhere if things go sideways.

    1. Injury and performance risk. All things considered, Skubal is a pretty safe bet on a long-term contract, though he is a pitcher, and pitchers get hurt. It's what they do. Skubal has had three elbow surgeries, including Tommy John surgery in 2017 and a minor procedure this May. If he gets hurt again, or his performance slips for whatever reason, then he could wind up costing himself in the big picture because he won't be able to opt out and sign a larger deal. A short-term, high-dollar contract will pay him handsomely. He won't struggle to put bread on the table. But injury/performance risk means Skubal could ultimately leave money on the table.

    In a recent development, 2. Potential salary cap. It is possible the next CBA will include a salary cap, which could limit Skubal's market and earning potential should he go back out into free agency in a year or two (or three). It's not just the cap itself either. MLB has proposed contract limits as part of the salary cap: five years at 15% of the cap for players who change teams, or six years at 16% of the cap for players who remain with their current team. Even if MLB doesn't get a salary cap and instead the competitive balance tax system remains in place with stiffer penalties, that could cost Skubal in the future. This offseason might be his last chance to sign in a truly free market.

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light.
    • In a recent development, how have they turned things around?
    • Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light. It initially came against weaker opponents, with wins over the Pacers, Clippers, Jazz and Kings getting them back near .500. But these back-to-back wins over Cleveland (on Friday) and Detroit (on Saturday) put a real stamp on this stretch. After all the panic, Miami has won seven of nine and is tied for the East's No. 4 seed entering this week.

    In a recent development, how have they turned things around? Let's take a look at four major reasons.

    Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins. The concerns over their offensive fit -- as relative non-shooters who operate largely in the same spots -- have quieted, but also a good bit of this production is coming independent of one another as Erik Spoelstra is staggering their minutes between the start of each half and fourth-quarter closing time.

    With shooters all around, Adebayo and Antetokounmpo are free to attack maximum interior space and exploit soft midrange spots, which has been the bread and butter of this run.

    Every mid range jumper from Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo against Cleveland last night: pic.twitter.com/jeamVaSLhk.

    As pointed out by Couper Moorhead of NBA.com, the Heat face more drop-coverage defense (when the major who's guarding the ball screener falls back toward the rim rather than stepping up to the level of the screen or even higher to contest the shooter coming off the screen) than any other offense in the league. That's because nobody fears Miami's pull-up 3-point shooters, and because Giannis and Bam are such forceful attackers of the rim.

    The soft spot is in between, outside the restricted circle but inside the 3-point line, or even better inside the free-throw line. It's the dreaded midrange zone, where defenses are happy to, concede shots to players like Giannis and Bam, and right now they are both knocking these supposedly inefficient looks down at ridiculous rates.

    These are by far career-high percentages for both guys, and they are coming on career-high frequencies from these zones (over 30% of their total shot attempts in the 3-10 range). Over these last nine games, Giannis is a scorching 22 for 33 from 10-19 feet while Adebayo -- who has also been the best post scorer in the league at 1.26 PPP on 4.8 post-ups per game -- is 30 for 44 from 5-14 feet.

    They are absolutely wearing these outer-paint shots out, and if defenses keep with the drop coverage, these shots are likely to remain consistently available. It's not to say they'll keep making them at this rate, of course. But to have established these go-zones is a significant step for Miami's half-court offense, because we all know how dangerous they are in the open floor as the highest-frequency and second-highest-scoring transition team.

    Now add in the fact that Miami kills teams on the glass with Giannis and Bam on the court (over these last nine, they are grabbing 78.7 percent of all available defensive rebounds and 37.8% of all offensive rebounds, both of which would lead the league), and in the turnover battle, and what you have is a Heat team that is getting a lot more true shot attempts than its opponents (almost 10 more per 100 possessions).

    It has been revealed that that is everything in today's possession-obsessed NBA. Get up more shots than your opponent by generating second-chance opportunities on the offensive boards and by creating more turnovers than you cough up, and you're in a good spot. Make those extra shots at the rate Miami is right now, and you're almost unbeatable.

    Industry observers note that mitchell has gone from a guy perhaps playing to stay in the league, or at least in an NBA rotation, to a current top-three Most Improved Player candidate at FanDuel (+900). He's blowing his previous production away.

    According to recent reports, the Heat are a low-volume pick-and-roll team for the same reasons they're a prime candidate for drop coverage: They don't have those kinds of pull-up shooters. Mitchell can punish drops with pull-up 3s on occasion (8 for 20 so far, per Synergy), but more importantly he's the one most often hitting Bam and Giannis in those soft-pocket midrange spots we talked about -- in addition to the rim rolls, cuts and kick-out 3s that open up as he breaches the paint, often in transition.

    It has been revealed that of Mitchell's 119 assists so far, 55 have gone to Giannis and Bam, and he has directly set up a 3-point make 37 times. Those 9.2 assists per game lead the league among qualified players, and the 257 points his assists have generated rank second only to Trae Young's 260, per PBP Stats. Young is making $49 million this year. Mitchell is making $12 million.

    According to recent reports, then there is the shooting. Mitchell has steadily improved from range throughout his career, but this season he's on fire at 43% on catch-and-shoot 3s, per Synergy, as part of Miami's spacing around Bam and Giannis. We saw all of Mitchell's tools in his 22-point/17-assist masterpiece against Cleveland.

    Davion Mitchell ABSURD statline vs Cavs: 22 PTS | 5 REB | 17 AST | 7/14 FG | 66 TS% pic.twitter.com/b0d8I1XHDy.

    Recent findings suggest that thompson isn't the player he was in his prime. His defense has especially declined, and he's not going to be putting up any more 37-point quarters. But he's still a sniper.

    Thompson is splashing 42% on almost 10 3s a game, and his 48 total 3-pointers rank third league-wide, and his 15.3 PPG are the most he's averaged since leaving Golden State. He's been especially hot of late, averaging 20 PPG on 48/45 shooting splits over his last seven games.

    Klay Thompson was amazing vs the Pistons26 PTS - 4 AST - 6 3PM - 10/17 FGM Found a upcoming home pic.twitter.com/JvQju9Hais.

    Over the last seven games, Miami is plus-11.7 with Thompson on the court and minus-3.7 when he's off. That's the best split on the team. The starting lineup of Mitchell, Bam, Giannis, Thompson and Pelle Larsson (who has been major in this turnaround, too, since his promotion to the first five), the Heat are outscoring opponents by 23 points per 100 possessions, and Thompson has been particularly effective playing alongside Giannis. With those two on the court as Bam rests, Miami is drumming teams by 31.6 points per 100, per Databallr.

    Miami's defense was expected to be a strength, and when people looked up and saw a bottom-barrel rating, it was jarring. Some of that, if not most of it, could be attributed to inordinately hot shooting by their opponents, which wasn't likely to continue. And indeed it hasn't.

    Through the first seven games, Miami opponents were shooting 41.8% from 3 and 50% from the midrange, per Cleaning the Glass. That made for a 58.7 effective field-goal percentage, despite Miami's defense registering a top-three expected eFG% (52.9) based on the shots they were surrendering, per Cleaning the Glass.

    Recent findings suggest that translation: the Heat were, and are, forcing generally inefficient shots, but to start the year those shots were going in at a rate of almost 6% better than expected. That was the worst, or unluckiest, mark in the league, however you want to look at it.

    Industry observers note that cut to this four-game win streak, over which opponents are down to 35.2% from 3 with a 53.9 eFG% against an expected 54%, per CTG. That's in part because Miami has cut the number of wide-open 3s (nearest defender at least six feet away) it was allowing to start the year almost in half (to start, they were surrendering 16 wide-open 3s every night, but over this four-game winning streak they are down to 9.1, stingiest in the league). Even better, their opponents have come down from a 45.5% conversion rate on those wide-open 3s to 40%.

    Industry observers note that all of which is to say, Miami's opponent shooting is coming back to earth. Hot shooting can render any defense helpless, but over time, if you're forcing a team into tough shots from tough spots, the averages are going to swing back your way eventually. Miami is starting to see that happen.

    The Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet. It does not appear a trade is imminent. We ranked Marte among the offseason's top trade candidates despite his odd AWOL incidents the last few seasons. Even at 33, he remains one of the game's best second basemen.

    The Blue Jays went 79-83 this past season largely because of their offense, which ranked dead last in runs and home runs. They also ranked 17th in WAR at second base as All-Star Ernie Clement ran out of steam in the second half. Offensively, Marte is coming off his worst 162-game season since 2018, though he would still represent a clear upgrade for the Blue Jays.

    In a recent development, the Giants continue to decline trade calls about ace righty Logan Webb, reports USA Today. Webb, 30 next week, had his worst full season in the big leagues in 2026, in part due to a nagging knee injury, though he is signed affordably through 2028. San Francisco needs to add to its rotation, not subtract one of the game's best and most durable starters.

    In a recent development, that mentioned, a Webb trade would presumably net the Giants multiple young players and improve the team's talent base. It never hurts to listen, but for now, the Giants seem disinclined to move their best pitcher since Madison Bumgarner was in his prime. Webb and Landen Roupp are the only locks for San Francisco's 2027 rotation at the moment.

    It has been revealed that not surprisingly, the Braves want to add at least one starting pitcher, according to The Athletic. They could also re-sign Raisel Iglesias or bring in another late-inning reliever even after signing Phillips. Chris Sale and Grant Holmes are Atlanta's only returning healthy starters. Bryce Elder (knee), Spencer Schwellenbach (elbow) and Spencer Strider (elbow) all finished the season injured.

    According to recent reports, the Braves will give Didier Fuentes, who was so dominant as a reliever this past season, a chance to start in 2027. It will be difficult to count on him for a full season, however. Fuentes, 21, threw a career-high 97 innings between the minors, majors, and postseason in 2026. Atlanta will need to monitor his workload next year. Another starter to soak up innings is a must this offseason.

    According to recent reports, the Tigers have interest in free agent left-hander Shota Imanaga, reports MLB.com. Jackson Jobe, Troy Melton, River Ryan, and Framber Valdez are presumably locks for Detroit's rotation. Ty Madden and Keider Montero are depth options. Reese Olson is expected back from shoulder surgery early next year. Still, the Tigers could clearly use another starting pitcher.

    According to recent reports, we ranked Imanaga, 33, as the 30th-best free agent available this offseason. He has been very home run prone the last two years (1.9 homers per nine innings), which could make him a good match for what is now called Fifth Third Park. Detroit's stadium tends to play pitcher-friendly, particularly in April and September (and October), when the ball doesn't carry well in the cold.

    Recent findings suggest that the Blue Jays are receiving calls about infielder Ernie Clement and utility man Davis Schneider, reports The Athletic. Teams have also inquired about catcher Brandon Valenzuela, who was a Gold Glove finalist as a rookie in 2026. Toronto reportedly has interest in Jazz Chisholm Jr. as it seeks more of a power bat on the infield, potentially making Clement expendable.

    Schneider, 27, had a poor 2026 and spent time in Triple-A, though he is versatile and has hit lefties in spots over the years. There is a shocking shortage of quality right-handed bats throughout baseball right now. Schneider's heavy plate discipline approach and ability to play left field as well as some infield positions make him an interesting enough target this offseason.

    The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox are among several teams pursuing Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Taira, 26, had a 1.36 ERA in 145 innings for the Seibu Lions in 2026. We ranked him as the 19th-best free agent available this offseason, though he could ultimately wind up in the bullpen given his height (5-foot-8).

    The Padres and two Chicago teams need starting pitching this offseason (they need multiple starters, really) and would likely use Taira in their rotation, at least to begin the season. For what it's worth, Taira told Sanspo he does not have a preferred destination, geographically. The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox would all give him a chance to pitch for a contender right away.

    In a recent development, the Cardinals have declined trade inquiries into first baseman Alec Burleson and shortstop Masyn Winn, according to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. St. Louis is also receiving interest in catchers Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés, who are more likely to be traded. Burleson and Winn are off-limits, though, and considered part of the long-term future in St. Louis.

    Recent findings suggest that leo Bernal, who was so impressive during his September call up, and top prospect Rainiel Rodriguez are the future behind the plate for the Cardinals. Pagés is a traditional glove-first backup catcher. Crooks has some offensive upside thanks to his hard-hit ability (exit velocity, etc.), and he rates well as a pitch-framer and thrower. He's an appealing target for catcher-needy teams.

    What's next for Red Sox after Jake Bauers deal? Plus more intel from the MLB GM Meetings

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (875 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports
